Introduction

Zinc is a focused web framework on top of net/http. The current core is intentionally small: routing, middleware, request binding, response helpers, files, and explicit server lifecycle.


That keeps Zinc close to the standard library. Your app is still an http.Handler, handlers still return error, and optional behavior like rendering, validation, or custom JSON encoding is configured through Config instead of hidden framework-only machinery.

What Zinc Gives You

  • Express-style route patterns like /users/:id and /files/*path
  • One handler shape for routes and middleware: func(*zinc.Context) error
  • Route groups, prefix middleware, automatic HEAD / OPTIONS, and route metadata through c.FullPath() and c.Route()
  • Binding helpers for path, query, header, JSON, XML, and form data
  • Response helpers for JSON, XML, HTML, streams, redirects, files, attachments, and rendering
  • Explicit startup and shutdown via Listen, Serve, and Shutdown

The Shape Of A Zinc App

package main

import (
  "log"

  "github.com/0mjs/zinc"
)

func main() {
  app := zinc.New()

  app.Get("/health", func(c *zinc.Context) error {
    return c.String("ok")
  })

  api := app.Group("/api")
  api.Get("/users/:id", func(c *zinc.Context) error {
    return c.JSON(zinc.Map{
      "id":        c.Param("id"),
      "full_path": c.FullPath(),
      "method":    c.Route().Method,
    })
  })

  log.Fatal(app.Listen(":8080"))
}

Small Core, Clear Extension Points

Zinc does not try to be every subsystem in your application. If you want validation, rendering, custom JSON encoding, or bespoke error handling, wire those through NewWithConfig. If you want focused middleware, use separate packages like middleware/cors or mount standard net/http handlers directly.
